features.name: Device Reset
features.description:
## Device Reset (F_DEVICE_RESET)

**Purpose:** Device Reset provides a hardware mechanism to force the e•MMC device back to a known initial state (Pre-idle state), enabling the host to recover from error conditions or reinitialize the device without power cycling.

**Behavior:** When the RST_n signal is asserted by the host, the device terminates any ongoing operations and returns to the Pre-idle state, clearing internal state machines and preparing for a fresh initialization sequence. This is a fundamental P0 (highest priority) initialization feature that serves as the entry point for all device initialization flows, including normal boot operations and error recovery scenarios as described in sections 6.3.1 and 6.4.1 of the specification.

features.name: Device Initialization Process
features.description:
## Device Initialization Process (F_DEVICE_INIT)

The Device Initialization Process defines the complete sequence of operations required to bring an e•MMC device from power-on or reset state to a fully operational condition where data transfers can occur. This P0-priority feature encompasses device reset procedures (section 6.4.1), transitioning from busy to ready state (section 6.4.3), and the device identification process (section 6.4.4) where the host discovers and configures connected e•MMC devices. As a foundational initialization feature, it establishes the communication protocol, validates access modes for devices larger than 2GB, and assigns relative device addresses (RCA) before the device can enter data transfer mode.

features.name: Device Identification Process
features.description:
## Device Identification Process (F_DEVICE_IDENT)

Based on the specification reference to **section 6.4.4 (Device identification process)**, this feature implements the protocol sequence where the host assigns a unique Relative Card Address (RCA) to each e•MMC device on the bus. During this process, the host issues CMD2 to retrieve the device's unique Card Identification (CID) register, followed by CMD3 to assign the RCA, which transitions the device from Identification State to Stand-by State. This mandatory P0 initialization step establishes the addressing mechanism required for all subsequent device-specific communication in data transfer mode.

features.name: Operating Condition Validation
features.description:
## Operating Condition Validation (F_OP_COND_VALID)

**Purpose:** This feature validates that the host and e•MMC device can operate under compatible voltage and access mode conditions during the initialization sequence, primarily through the CMD1 (SEND_OP_COND) exchange.

**Behavior:** During initialization, the host sends CMD1 with its supported voltage range and access mode requirements, and the device responds with its OCR (Operating Conditions Register) indicating supported voltages and whether it supports sector addressing (for devices >2GB). The validation process iterates until the device signals ready (busy bit cleared) and confirms mutual operating condition agreement, as described in sections 6.4.2 (Access mode validation) and 6.4.3 (From busy to ready). This P0-priority feature is essential for establishing proper communication parameters before proceeding with device identification.

features.name: e•MMC Bus Protocol
features.description:
## e•MMC Bus Protocol (F_BUS_PROTOCOL)

The e•MMC Bus Protocol defines the fundamental communication mechanism between the host controller and the e•MMC device, governing how commands, responses, and data are transmitted over the bus interface. This protocol specifies the signaling conventions, timing requirements, and handshaking procedures that enable reliable data exchange across the CMD and DAT lines in various bus width configurations (1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit modes). As a P0 priority feature, it forms the essential foundation upon which all higher-level operations such as device identification, data transfers, and boot operations depend.

**Reference Specification Sections:** 5.3.1 (Bus Protocol), 6.6 (Data transfer mode), 6.6.6 (Bus testing procedure)

features.name: Bus Speed Mode Support
features.description:
## Bus Speed Mode Support (F_SPEED_MODES)

**Purpose:** This foundational feature defines the various bus speed modes supported by the e•MMC device, which determine the maximum data transfer rates achievable between the host and device. As specified in section 5.4, e•MMC supports multiple speed modes including legacy, High-Speed, and HS200, each with different timing characteristics and throughput capabilities.

**Behavior:** The device advertises its supported speed modes in the EXT_CSD register, and the host selects an appropriate mode during initialization using the procedures defined in sections 6.6.2-6.6.4. Higher speed modes like HS200 require specific bus width configurations, voltage levels, and may necessitate sampling tuning sequences (section 6.6.7) to ensure reliable data transfer at elevated frequencies.

features.name: Backwards Compatibility Mode
features.description:
## Backwards Compatibility Mode (F_BACKWARD_COMPAT)

**Purpose:** Backwards Compatibility Mode ensures that e•MMC devices can operate with legacy host controllers by supporting older, slower bus speed modes alongside newer high-speed modes like HS200.

**Behavior:** This mode allows e•MMC devices to fall back to standard speed (up to 26 MHz) or high-speed (up to 52 MHz) operation when connected to hosts that do not support advanced timing modes. The device automatically negotiates the highest mutually supported speed mode during initialization, ensuring interoperability across different generations of e•MMC hosts while maintaining the option to leverage faster modes when available. This is designated P0 priority as it is fundamental to ensuring broad device compatibility across the e•MMC ecosystem.

features.name: High Speed Mode
features.description:
## High Speed Mode (F_HIGH_SPEED)

High Speed Mode is a legacy bus speed mode that enables data transfer rates up to 52 MHz clock frequency, supporting throughput of up to 52 MB/s in single data rate (SDR) operation on an 8-bit bus. This mode is selected by writing to the HS_TIMING field in the EXT_CSD register (typically setting it to 0x1), transitioning the device from the default backwards-compatible mode to higher performance operation.

As a foundational speed mode (P0 priority), High Speed Mode serves as a stepping stone between legacy compatibility mode and the more advanced HS200/HS400 modes, and is commonly used during initialization sequences or in systems that don't require the maximum performance of newer timing modes.

features.name: HS200 Bus Speed Mode
features.description:
## HS200 Bus Speed Mode (F_HS200)

**Purpose:** HS200 Bus Speed Mode is a high-speed interface mode that enables data transfer rates up to 200 MB/s using a 200 MHz clock frequency on a single-ended 8-bit or 4-bit data bus operating at 1.8V signaling levels.

**Behavior:** This mode requires the host to perform a sampling tuning sequence (as defined in section 6.6.7.1) to calibrate the optimal data sampling point, compensating for signal timing variations across the interface. HS200 operates with source-synchronous clocking where the device transmits data aligned to the clock edges, and the host must implement an adjustable sampling mechanism to reliably capture data at these high frequencies. Selection of HS200 mode is accomplished through the mode selection procedure defined in section 6.6.4, which involves configuring the appropriate fields in the Extended CSD register.

features.name: Dual Data Rate Mode
features.description:
## Dual Data Rate Mode (F_DDR)

Dual Data Rate (DDR) Mode is a high-speed bus operation mode where data is transferred on both the rising and falling edges of the clock signal, effectively doubling the data throughput compared to Single Data Rate (SDR) modes at the same clock frequency. In e•MMC systems, DDR modes (such as DDR52) operate with a 52MHz clock but achieve data rates equivalent to 104MHz SDR operation by sampling data on both clock edges.

This mode requires specific timing configurations set through the EXT_CSD register and typically operates with either 4-bit or 8-bit bus widths, enabling maximum theoretical throughput of 52MB/s (4-bit) or 104MB/s (8-bit) in DDR52 mode.

features.name: Bus Width Selection (1/4/8-bit)
features.description:
## Bus Width Selection (1/4/8-bit) (F_BUS_WIDTH)

**Purpose:** This feature enables the host to configure the data bus width between the host controller and eMMC device, selecting from 1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit parallel data transfer modes to optimize throughput based on system capabilities and power requirements.

**Behavior:** Bus width selection is performed by writing to the BUS_WIDTH field in the EXT_CSD register using CMD6 (SWITCH command). The device defaults to 1-bit mode after power-up/reset, and the host must explicitly switch to wider bus modes (4-bit or 8-bit) after device identification. The bus testing procedure (CMD19/CMD14) can be used to verify proper connectivity before committing to a wider bus configuration, ensuring reliable data transfer across all active data lines.

features.name: Bus Testing Procedure
features.description:
## Bus Testing Procedure (F_BUS_TESTING)

The Bus Testing Procedure is a mechanism that allows the host to verify the integrity and proper connection of the data bus lines between the host controller and the e•MMC device. The host sends a specific test pattern using CMD19 (BUSTEST_W) and reads it back using CMD14 (BUSTEST_R), comparing the returned pattern to detect any stuck, shorted, or improperly connected data lines. This procedure is typically performed during initialization before selecting the final bus width (1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit) to ensure reliable data transfer across all active data lines.

features.name: Data Transfer Mode
features.description:
## Data Transfer Mode (F_DATA_TRANSFER)

**Purpose:** Data Transfer Mode is the primary operational state of an e•MMC device where actual data read and write operations occur between the host and the device's memory partitions.

**Behavior:** After completing device identification and initialization, the e•MMC enters Data Transfer Mode where it can execute block read/write commands, configure bus speed modes (including high-speed and HS200), select power classes, perform bus width selection (1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit), and execute memory management operations such as erase, TRIM, sanitize, and secure erase functions. This mode encompasses all runtime data operations and performance optimizations including sampling tuning sequences for high-speed interfaces.

features.name: Data Read
features.description:
## F_DATA_READ (Data Read)

**Purpose:** This feature defines the fundamental data read operations for transferring data from the e•MMC device to the host controller during normal data transfer mode.

**Behavior:** Data Read operations enable the host to retrieve stored data from the e•MMC device using block read commands (such as CMD17 for single block and CMD18 for multiple block reads). The feature supports configurable block lengths, handles data transfer across the selected bus width (1-bit, 4-bit, or 8-bit), and manages the data transfer protocol including CRC checking for data integrity verification. As a P0 priority feature under Data Transfer, it represents a core capability essential for all e•MMC system operations.

features.name: Data Write
features.description:
## F_DATA_WRITE (Data Write)

**Purpose:** This feature implements the fundamental data write operations for transferring data from the host to the e•MMC device's non-volatile memory, enabling persistent storage of user data and system information.

**Behavior:** Data Write operations utilize block write commands (such as CMD24 for single block and CMD25 for multiple block writes) to transfer data across the bus in 512-byte block units, with the device managing internal flash programming sequences including wear leveling and error correction. As a P0 priority feature under F_DATA_TRANSFER, it is essential for all e•MMC implementations and must support various bus widths and speed modes while properly handling busy signaling during the internal programming phase.

features.name: Reliable Write
features.description:
## Reliable Write (F_RELIABLE_WRITE)

**Purpose:** Reliable Write is a data integrity feature that guarantees atomic write operations to the e•MMC device, ensuring that data is either completely written to non-volatile memory or not written at all in case of power failure or system reset.

**Behavior:** When enabled, the device ensures that write data is committed to non-volatile storage before signaling completion, protecting against partial writes that could corrupt data during unexpected power loss. This feature can be configured on a per-partition basis through the EXT_CSD register (EUDA_EN, ENHA_1-4 bits) or enabled for individual write operations using the Reliable Write bit in CMD23 (SET_BLOCK_COUNT), making it essential for critical system data like file system metadata and boot configurations.

features.name: Packed Commands
features.description:
## Packed Commands (F_PACKED_CMD)

**Purpose:** Packed Commands is a data transfer optimization feature that allows the host to bundle multiple read or write commands into a single command sequence, reducing command overhead and improving overall throughput efficiency.

**Behavior:** Instead of issuing individual commands for each data transfer operation, the host constructs a "packed command header" that describes multiple block read or write operations, then sends them together in one transaction. This minimizes the latency associated with command-response cycles and is particularly beneficial for workloads involving many small, sequential transfers, enabling more efficient use of the e•MMC bus bandwidth in high-speed modes.

features.name: Erase Operations
features.description:
## Erase Operations (F_ERASE)

Erase Operations provide the fundamental mechanism for clearing data from e•MMC storage by resetting memory cells to a defined state (either '0' or '1' depending on device configuration). This feature encompasses the core erase command sequence (CMD35/CMD36 for setting erase start/end addresses, followed by CMD38) that operates on erase groups—the minimum erasable unit defined by the device. As a P0 priority feature, erase operations are essential for storage management, wear leveling support, and preparing memory regions for new data writes with potentially improved write performance.

features.name: Trim Operation
features.description:
## Trim Operation (F_TRIM)

**Purpose:** The Trim operation provides an efficient mechanism for the host to inform the eMMC device that specific data blocks are no longer needed and can be marked as invalid, allowing the device's internal garbage collection to reclaim and optimize those flash memory regions.

**Behavior:** Unlike a full erase operation, Trim does not immediately remove data but rather marks the specified address ranges as candidates for erasure during the device's background operations. This enables faster host-side completion while allowing the eMMC controller to optimize write amplification and wear leveling by handling the actual physical erasure asynchronously, improving overall device performance and longevity.

features.name: Secure Erase
features.description:
## Secure Erase (F_SECURE_ERASE)

**Purpose:** Secure Erase is a security-enhanced erase operation that permanently and irreversibly removes data from specified address ranges, ensuring that the erased data cannot be recovered even through advanced forensic techniques or direct NAND flash analysis.

**Behavior:** Unlike standard erase operations that may simply mark blocks as available without physically removing data, Secure Erase guarantees complete data destruction by overwriting or physically clearing the underlying flash memory cells. This operation is initiated after defining the erase range using ERASE_GROUP_START and ERASE_GROUP_END commands, followed by an ERASE command with the secure erase bit set in the argument. The operation typically takes longer than standard erase due to the additional steps required to ensure data unrecoverability, and the device reports completion through the busy signal on the DAT0 line.

**Security Context:** This feature addresses data sanitization requirements for applications handling sensitive information, providing cryptographic-grade data destruction that meets security compliance standards when devices are decommissioned, repurposed, or returned.

features.name: Secure Trim
features.description:
## Secure Trim (F_SECURE_TRIM)

**Description:**
Secure Trim is a two-step security operation that combines the functionality of Trim with secure data removal, ensuring that trimmed data blocks cannot be recovered through any means. The operation first marks specified blocks for trimming (using CMD35/CMD36 to set start/end addresses), then executes a secure purge operation that physically removes the data from the NAND flash, including any copies in the device's internal buffers or unmapped regions. This feature is essential for applications requiring certified data sanitization, such as enterprise security or regulatory compliance scenarios where sensitive data must be irreversibly destroyed.

**Parent Feature:** F_ERASE - Inherits base erase command infrastructure while adding cryptographic-level data destruction guarantees.

features.name: Sanitize Operation
features.description:
## Sanitize Operation (F_SANITIZE)

**Purpose:** The Sanitize operation provides a security-focused mechanism to permanently remove all data from unmapped user data addresses, ensuring that previously erased, trimmed, or discarded data cannot be recovered through any means, including direct physical access to the flash memory.

**Behavior:** When initiated via EXT_CSD register, Sanitize forces the device to physically erase all copies of data that were previously marked for deletion by Erase, TRIM, or Discard commands but may still exist in the underlying flash memory. Unlike basic erase operations that may only unmap logical addresses, Sanitize guarantees cryptographic-level data destruction by ensuring no residual data patterns remain in the NAND cells, making it essential for secure data disposal in applications handling sensitive information.

features.name: Write Protection Management
features.description:
## Write Protection Management (F_WRITE_PROTECT)

**Purpose:** This feature provides comprehensive management of write protection mechanisms across the e•MMC device, enabling hosts to protect critical data regions from accidental or unauthorized modification.

**Behavior:** Write Protection Management encompasses multiple protection schemes including temporary (power-on) write protection, permanent write protection, and boot partition write protection (as referenced in section 6.3.7). The feature allows hosts to configure write-protect groups, query protection status via EXT_CSD registers, and apply different protection levels to user data areas and boot partitions to safeguard firmware, boot code, and other critical system data from being overwritten.

features.name: Boot Operation
features.description:
## Boot Operation (F_BOOT_MODE)

Boot Operation enables the e•MMC device to provide boot data to the host system immediately after power-up or hardware reset, before the normal device identification process completes. The device enters a special boot mode where it automatically streams data from dedicated boot partitions (Boot Area Partition 1 or 2) when it detects specific signaling conditions on the CMD line during the pre-idle state. This P0-priority feature is essential for system initialization, allowing processors to fetch critical boot code directly from the e•MMC with configurable bus width and timing parameters, supporting both standard and alternative boot sequences as defined in section 6.3.

features.name: Alternative Boot Operation
features.description:
## Alternative Boot Operation (F_ALT_BOOT)

**Purpose:** Alternative Boot Operation provides a secondary method for initiating boot mode on e•MMC devices, allowing the host to retrieve boot data through a different signaling sequence than the standard boot operation.

**Behavior:** In alternative boot operation, the host initiates boot mode by asserting the CMD line low while keeping CS (chip select) high, rather than using the standard boot acknowledge sequence. This method provides flexibility for systems where the primary boot mechanism may not be suitable, while still accessing the same boot partition data. The device responds by streaming boot data from the designated boot partition (Boot Area Partition 1 or 2) to the host, enabling system initialization without requiring full device identification.

**Reference:** See section 6.3.4 (Alternative boot operation) for detailed timing and protocol requirements.

features.name: Partitioning
features.description:
## F_PARTITIONING (Partitioning)

**Purpose:** This feature enables the division of e•MMC storage into multiple logical partitions, including boot partitions, general purpose partitions, and the user data area, allowing for organized storage management and dedicated areas for specific functions like boot code.

**Behavior:** Partitioning is configured through Extended CSD registers and allows creation of up to four General Purpose Partitions with configurable sizes and attributes (such as enhanced reliability). Once partitions are configured and the partitioning setting is completed (typically a one-time operation), the host accesses specific partitions by setting the PARTITION_ACCESS field in EXT_CSD, with each partition appearing as an independent addressable storage area starting from address 0.

features.name: Boot Area Partitions
features.description:
## Boot Area Partitions (F_BOOT_PARTITION)

Boot Area Partitions are two dedicated, fixed-size memory regions (Boot Area Partition 1 and Boot Area Partition 2) within the e•MMC device specifically designed to store boot code that the host processor retrieves during system initialization. These partitions support special boot operation modes where the device can automatically output boot data upon power-up or reset without requiring standard command sequences, enabling faster and more reliable system boot. The boot partitions are separate from the user data area and can be independently write-protected, with configurable size (typically 128KB to 16MB each) set during device manufacturing or initial configuration via the EXT_CSD register.

features.name: General Purpose Partitions
features.description:
## General Purpose Partitions (F_GP_PARTITION)

General Purpose Partitions are user-configurable storage areas within the e•MMC device that can be created during the partition configuration process, separate from the default User Data Area and Boot Partitions. These partitions (typically up to 4 GP partitions designated GP1-GP4) allow system designers to allocate dedicated storage regions with specific attributes such as enhanced reliability or write protection, enabling isolation of different data types or system components. Once configured via the EXT_CSD registers during the partitioning setup phase, GP partitions are accessed by switching the PARTITION_ACCESS field, and their sizes and attributes become permanent after the partition configuration is completed (OTP operation).

features.name: Enhanced User Data Area
features.description:
## Enhanced User Data Area (F_ENH_AREA)

The Enhanced User Data Area feature allows a portion of the User Data Area partition to be configured with enhanced reliability attributes, typically providing higher endurance or data retention characteristics similar to SLC (Single-Level Cell) storage. This enhanced region is defined by specifying a start address and size during the one-time partition configuration process, and once set, the device treats this area with elevated reliability parameters compared to standard MLC/TLC storage.

As a child feature of F_PARTITIONING, this capability is configured through the EXT_CSD registers (ENH_START_ADDR and ENH_SIZE_MULT) and is part of the overall partition management scheme described in section 6.2, enabling system designers to allocate critical data storage areas that require maximum reliability within the user data space.

features.name: Replay Protected Memory Block
features.description:
## Replay Protected Memory Block (RPMB)

**Purpose:** The Replay Protected Memory Block (RPMB) is a dedicated secure partition within the e•MMC device that provides authenticated and replay-protected access to stored data, preventing unauthorized modification or replay attacks on sensitive information such as cryptographic keys, secure counters, or DRM-related data.

**Behavior:** RPMB uses a shared secret key (authentication key) and a monotonic write counter to authenticate all read and write operations through HMAC-SHA256 signatures, ensuring that each transaction is unique and cannot be replayed by an attacker. The host must provide valid authentication for write operations, and the device signs read responses, enabling mutual verification of data integrity and authenticity between the host and the e•MMC device.

features.name: Interrupt Mode
features.description:
## Interrupt Mode (F_INTERRUPT_MODE)

**Purpose:** Interrupt Mode enables an e•MMC device to signal the host when it requires attention or has completed an operation, allowing for efficient asynchronous communication without requiring the host to continuously poll the device status.

**Behavior:** As defined in section 6.5, this mode allows the device to assert an interrupt signal to notify the host of events such as data ready conditions, operation completion, or error states. This mechanism improves system efficiency by freeing the host processor from busy-waiting loops, enabling power-efficient operation particularly important in embedded and mobile applications where the e•MMC standard is commonly deployed.

features.name: High Priority Interrupt
features.description:
## High Priority Interrupt (HPI)

**Purpose:** The High Priority Interrupt feature allows a host to interrupt and halt an ongoing e•MMC device operation (such as a long write, erase, or background operation) to execute a higher-priority read or write command with minimal latency.

**Behavior:** When the host issues an HPI command (CMD12 or CMD13 with HPI bit set), the device suspends its current operation, saves its state, and becomes ready to accept the urgent command. After the high-priority operation completes, the original operation can be resumed, ensuring that time-critical data access requirements are met without waiting for lengthy operations to complete naturally. This is particularly valuable in systems requiring real-time responsiveness while performing maintenance operations like garbage collection or large block erases.

features.name: Background Operations
features.description:
## Background Operations (F_BKOPS)

Background Operations (BKOPS) is a critical maintenance feature that allows the e•MMC device to perform internal housekeeping tasks such as garbage collection, wear leveling, and block management during periods when the host is not actively accessing the device. The host can either manually trigger background operations by setting the BKOPS_START field in the Extended CSD register, or enable automatic background operations (AUTO_BKOPS) where the device self-initiates these tasks when idle. This feature is essential for maintaining optimal device performance and longevity, as it prevents performance degradation that would otherwise occur if the device had to perform these maintenance operations during active read/write commands.

features.name: Power Management
features.description:
## Power Management (F_POWER_MGMT)

**Purpose:** Power Management is a foundational P0 feature that governs the e•MMC device's power supply requirements, power sequencing, and power state transitions throughout all operational modes. This feature defines the voltage levels (VCCQ for I/O and VCC for core), power-up/power-down sequences, and the mechanisms for transitioning between active, idle, and sleep states to optimize energy consumption.

**Behavior:** The feature encompasses power class selection (section 6.6.5) which allows hosts to negotiate power consumption levels based on bus width and speed mode, ensuring the device operates within the host's power budget. It also manages the device's response to power cycling, including proper initialization sequences and maintaining data integrity during unexpected power loss scenarios.

features.name: Power Off Notification
features.description:
## Power Off Notification (F_POWER_OFF_NOTIFY)

**Purpose:** Power Off Notification is a mechanism that allows the host to inform the eMMC device before power is removed, enabling the device to complete any pending internal operations and safely flush cached data to non-volatile memory.

**Behavior:** When the host sets the POWER_OFF_NOTIFICATION field in the EXT_CSD register (typically to values like POWERED_ON, POWER_OFF_SHORT, or POWER_OFF_LONG), the device prepares for an orderly shutdown by completing write operations and ensuring data integrity. This feature is critical for preventing data corruption and reducing the risk of file system inconsistencies that could occur if power is abruptly removed while the device has uncommitted data in volatile cache buffers.

features.name: Sleep/Awake
features.description:
## Sleep/Awake (F_SLEEP_AWAKE)

The Sleep/Awake feature enables the e•MMC device to enter an ultra-low power sleep state while retaining all device configuration and state information, allowing rapid return to operational mode without requiring full re-initialization. This is controlled via the SLEEP_AWAKE bit in the EXT_CSD register, where the host issues CMD5 (SLEEP_AWAKE) to transition the device between sleep and standby states. As a P1 priority power management feature, it provides significant power savings for battery-operated systems during idle periods while maintaining faster wake-up times compared to full power-off cycles.

features.name: H/W Reset
features.description:
## H/W Reset (F_HW_RESET)

**Hardware Reset** is a dedicated reset mechanism that allows the host to force the e•MMC device into a known initial state (Pre-idle) via the RST_n pin, independent of the command bus. This P0-priority feature is essential for system recovery scenarios where the device becomes unresponsive to software commands or when the bus protocol enters an unrecoverable error state.

When asserted, the hardware reset signal bypasses normal command processing and immediately terminates all ongoing operations, returning the device to its power-on reset condition ready for re-initialization. This capability is configured via the RST_n_FUNCTION field in the Extended CSD register and must be enabled before it can be used.

Referenced spec sections: 6.3.1 (Device reset to Pre-idle state), 6.4.1 (Device reset)

features.name: Cache
features.description:
## F_CACHE - Cache Feature

**Purpose:** The Cache feature provides a volatile write cache buffer within the e•MMC device that allows the host to temporarily store write data in faster volatile memory before it is committed to non-volatile flash storage, significantly improving write performance for bursty workloads.

**Behavior:** When enabled via EXT_CSD register configuration, write operations are initially stored in the device's internal cache memory, allowing the device to acknowledge completion quickly while background operations flush data to flash. The host can explicitly flush the cache using CMD6 (SWITCH) to set FLUSH_CACHE, ensuring data persistence before critical operations or power-down sequences, which is essential since cached data may be lost on unexpected power loss.

features.name: Context Management
features.description:
## Context Management (F_CONTEXT_MGMT)

Context Management enables the e•MMC device to maintain multiple independent operational contexts, allowing the host to define and manage separate logical data streams or access patterns. This feature improves performance by letting the device optimize internal operations (such as garbage collection and wear leveling) based on the characteristics of different data contexts, such as sequential versus random access patterns.

The host can configure contexts with specific attributes and associate write operations with particular context IDs, enabling the device to group related data physically and reduce write amplification for workloads with distinct access behaviors.

features.name: Data Tagging
features.description:
## Data Tagging (F_DATA_TAG)

Data Tagging is an e•MMC feature that allows the host to mark specific data blocks with metadata tags, enabling the device to optimize storage management and data handling based on the tagged attributes. This mechanism helps the e•MMC controller make intelligent decisions about data placement, caching strategies, and garbage collection by distinguishing between different types of data (such as hot/cold data or data with specific retention requirements). The feature is typically configured through the EXT_CSD register and can improve overall device performance and endurance by allowing more efficient internal data organization.

features.name: Device Lock/Unlock
features.description:
## Device Lock/Unlock (F_LOCK_UNLOCK)

The Device Lock/Unlock feature provides password-based access control for the e•MMC device, allowing the host to lock the device with a user-defined password to prevent unauthorized data access. When locked, the device restricts read and write operations to the user data area until the correct password is provided to unlock it. This security mechanism protects sensitive data at the hardware level, and optionally supports a forced erase capability that allows unlocking a device when the password is forgotten by permanently erasing all user data.

features.name: Command Engine
features.description:
## Command Engine (F_CMD_ENGINE)

The Command Engine is the core processing unit responsible for receiving, decoding, and executing all commands sent from the host to the e•MMC device over the CMD line. It manages the complete command lifecycle including command parsing, CRC validation, state machine transitions, and response generation according to the e•MMC protocol. As a P0 (highest priority) feature, it forms the fundamental infrastructure that enables all device operations—from device identification and initialization through data transfer modes, supporting the full command set defined in the specification.

features.name: Basic Commands (Class 0/1)
features.description:
## F_BASIC_CMD: Basic Commands (Class 0/1)

**Purpose:** This feature implements the fundamental command classes (Class 0 and Class 1) that are mandatory for all e•MMC devices, providing essential operations for device identification, initialization, and basic data transfer setup.

**Behavior:** Class 0 commands include basic system commands such as GO_IDLE_STATE (CMD0), ALL_SEND_CID (CMD2), SET_RELATIVE_ADDR (CMD3), SELECT/DESELECT_CARD (CMD7), SEND_CSD (CMD9), SEND_CID (CMD10), and SEND_STATUS (CMD13) that handle device reset, identification, addressing, and status queries. Class 1 commands support stream read operations. These commands form the minimum required command set that must be processed by the command engine (F_CMD_ENGINE) before any advanced operations can occur, establishing the communication foundation between host and device during the device identification mode described in section 6.4.

features.name: Block Read Commands (Class 2)
features.description:
## Block Read Commands (Class 2) (F_READ_CMD)

**Purpose:** Block Read Commands (Class 2) implements the fundamental data read operations defined in the eMMC specification, enabling the host to retrieve data blocks from the device's memory array using commands such as CMD17 (READ_SINGLE_BLOCK) and CMD18 (READ_MULTIPLE_BLOCK).

**Behavior:** As described in section 6.6.9 (Data read) and 6.6.9.1 (Block read), this feature handles addressed read operations where the host specifies a starting block address and the device transfers the requested data blocks over the data bus. The command engine processes read commands, manages the data transfer protocol including CRC checking, and supports both single-block and multiple-block read operations with appropriate termination handling (CMD12 for open-ended transfers).

features.name: Block Write Commands (Class 4)
features.description:
## F_WRITE_CMD: Block Write Commands (Class 4)

### Purpose
This feature implements the Class 4 block write command set, which provides the fundamental data write operations for transferring data from the host to the e•MMC device's non-volatile memory. As a P0 priority feature under the command engine, it is essential for all write operations to the device.

### Technical Behavior
Based on section 6.6.10 (Data write) and 6.6.10.1 (Block write), this feature handles:

- **CMD24 (WRITE_BLOCK)**: Single block write operation transferring one data block to a specified address
- **CMD25 (WRITE_MULTIPLE_BLOCK)**: Multiple block write operation for sequential block transfers with improved throughput
- **CMD27 (PROGRAM_CSD)**: Programming of programmable CSD register bits

The write commands manage the complete write protocol including command issuance, data transfer on the DAT lines, CRC verification, device programming time (busy indication), and write status response. The feature must handle write protection checks, address validation for the current access mode (byte vs. sector addressing for >2GB devices), and proper busy state monitoring via the DAT0 line during internal programming operations.

features.name: Erase Commands (Class 5)
features.description:
## Erase Commands (Class 5) (F_ERASE_CMD)

**Purpose:** Implements the Class 5 command set for erase operations, enabling the host to mark and erase ranges of memory blocks on the e•MMC device through the ERASE_GROUP_START (CMD35), ERASE_GROUP_END (CMD36), and ERASE (CMD38) command sequence.

**Behavior:** The erase operation works in a three-step process: first setting the start address of the erase group, then setting the end address, and finally issuing the erase command to execute the operation. This feature supports multiple erase variants including standard erase, TRIM, Secure Erase, Secure Trim, and Discard operations as specified in sections 6.6.11-6.6.16, with the specific operation type determined by the argument passed to CMD38.

features.name: I/O Mode Commands (Class 9)
features.description:
## I/O Mode Commands (Class 9) (F_IO_CMD)

**Purpose:** Class 9 commands were historically defined for SDIO (Secure Digital I/O) functionality to support peripheral I/O operations, but in the e•MMC specification, these commands are typically not applicable or are reserved since e•MMC devices are pure memory storage devices without I/O peripheral capabilities.

**Behavior:** In the context of e•MMC, Class 9 I/O mode commands are generally not implemented as e•MMC focuses exclusively on embedded storage functionality rather than the I/O extension features found in SD cards with SDIO support. The command class exists in the command classification framework for compatibility with the broader MMC/SD command structure, but e•MMC hosts and devices do not utilize these commands for normal operation.

**Note:** This feature has P2 priority likely because it represents placeholder/reserved command space that must be recognized by the command engine but does not require active implementation for e•MMC compliance.

features.name: Lock Device Commands (Class 7)
features.description:
## Lock Device Commands (Class 7) (F_LOCK_CMD)

**Purpose:** Lock Device Commands (Class 7) implements the password-based device locking mechanism that allows hosts to protect e•MMC device content from unauthorized access. This security feature enables setting, clearing, and managing passwords that control whether the device will accept data access commands.

**Behavior:** The feature primarily uses CMD42 (LOCK_UNLOCK) to perform operations including setting a new password, clearing an existing password, locking the device, unlocking the device, and optionally forcing erase when the password is forgotten. When locked, the device rejects most data transfer commands while still responding to basic commands for identification and status. The lock state persists across power cycles, requiring the correct password to be supplied after each power-up before data access is permitted.

features.name: Application-Specific Commands (Class 8)
features.description:
## Application-Specific Commands (Class 8) (F_APP_CMD)

**Purpose:** Application-Specific Commands (Class 8) provides a mechanism for extending the standard e•MMC command set through a two-command sequence, where CMD55 (APP_CMD) signals that the next command will be an application-specific command (ACMD) rather than a standard command.

**Behavior:** When the host issues CMD55, it sets the APP_CMD status bit in the device, indicating that the immediately following command should be interpreted as an application-specific command. This class includes commands like ACMD41 (SD_SEND_OP_COND) inherited from SD compatibility, and provides a namespace for vendor-specific or extended functionality without conflicting with the standard command index space. If no command follows CMD55 or a standard command is issued instead, the APP_CMD state is cleared and normal command interpretation resumes.

features.name: Security Protocols (Class 10)
features.description:
## Security Protocols (Class 10) (F_SECURITY_CMD)

Security Protocols (Class 10) encompasses the command set dedicated to secure data operations on e•MMC devices, including **Secure Erase (CMD38 with secure argument)** and **Secure Trim** operations. These commands ensure that erased data cannot be recovered by physically overwriting the flash memory cells, rather than simply marking blocks as available for reuse. As a child of the Command Engine with P2 priority, this feature implements cryptographically secure data destruction methods that are essential for devices handling sensitive information and meeting data sanitization compliance requirements.

features.name: OCR Register
features.description:
## OCR Register (F_OCR_REGISTER)

The OCR (Operation Conditions Register) is a 32-bit register that stores the device's supported voltage ranges and access mode information, which the host queries during device initialization to ensure voltage compatibility. During the identification process, the device uses the OCR to communicate its operating voltage window (typically 2.7V-3.6V) and whether it supports sector addressing mode (required for devices larger than 2GB) versus byte addressing mode. This register is critical for the power-up sequence and CMD1 (SEND_OP_COND) handshake, where the host and device negotiate compatible operating conditions before proceeding with device identification.

features.name: CID Register
features.description:
## CID Register (F_CID_REGISTER)

The CID (Card Identification) Register is a 128-bit read-only register that contains unique device identification information, including the manufacturer ID, OEM/Application ID, product name, product revision, serial number, and manufacturing date. This register is programmed during device manufacturing and is used by the host during the device identification process (CMD2/CMD10) to uniquely identify each e•MMC device in the system. The CID is essential for device enumeration and allows hosts to distinguish between multiple devices and verify device authenticity.

features.name: CSD Register
features.description:
## CSD Register (F_CSD_REGISTER)

The Card-Specific Data (CSD) Register is a 128-bit register that contains essential device configuration parameters including card capacity, maximum data transfer rates, supported command classes, read/write block lengths, and timing specifications. This register is programmed during manufacturing and provides the host with critical information needed to properly configure communication parameters and understand the device's capabilities. The CSD is read by the host during device identification using CMD9 and remains fundamental for establishing proper data transfer operations, though many extended capabilities in modern e•MMC devices are now stored in the Extended CSD register.

features.name: Extended CSD Register
features.description:
## Extended CSD Register (F_EXT_CSD_REGISTER)

The Extended CSD Register is a 512-byte register that extends the standard CSD (Card Specific Data) register to provide additional device configuration parameters, capability information, and mode settings specific to e•MMC devices. It contains critical fields for configuring partitions, selecting bus speed modes (including HS200), setting power classes, and controlling advanced features like boot operations and write protection. As a P0 priority register, it is fundamental to e•MMC operation, accessed via CMD8 (SEND_EXT_CSD) for reading and CMD6 (SWITCH) for modifying writable fields.

features.name: RCA Register
features.description:
## RCA Register (F_RCA_REGISTER)

The RCA (Relative Card Address) Register is a 16-bit register that stores the unique device address assigned during the identification process, which is used by the host to address the specific e•MMC device in all subsequent communications after initialization. Unlike SD cards where the device proposes its own RCA, in e•MMC the host assigns this address using CMD3 (SET_RELATIVE_ADDR), and the device stores it in this register. The RCA is essential for transitioning the device from identification mode to data transfer mode and is used in addressed commands (ac and adtc type) to select and communicate with the specific device on the bus.

features.name: DSR Register
features.description:
## DSR Register (Driver Stage Register)

The DSR (Driver Stage Register) is an optional 16-bit configuration register in e•MMC devices that allows the host to optimize the device's output driver characteristics to match the electrical requirements of the specific bus environment. When implemented, the host can program this register to adjust parameters such as output driver strength and bus loading compensation, helping to improve signal integrity on systems with varying bus lengths or capacitive loads.

The presence of DSR capability is indicated in the CSD register, and if supported, the host uses CMD4 (SET_DSR) to configure the register value during the device identification process before entering data transfer mode.

features.name: Error Handling
features.description:
## Error Handling (F_ERROR_HANDLING)

Error Handling encompasses the comprehensive mechanisms defined in the e•MMC specification for detecting, reporting, and recovering from various error conditions during device operation. This includes command CRC errors, data CRC errors, timeout conditions, illegal command responses, address out-of-range errors, and write protect violations, all communicated through the device status register and response tokens.

As a P0 priority feature, robust error handling is fundamental to reliable e•MMC operation, enabling hosts to identify failed operations, implement appropriate retry strategies, and maintain data integrity across all bus speed modes and operational states.

features.name: Speed Class / Performance
features.description:
## F_SPEED_CLASS: Speed Class / Performance

**Purpose:** This feature defines the performance classification and speed capabilities of the e•MMC device, encompassing the various bus speed modes (such as HS200) and associated timing parameters that determine data transfer rates between the host and device.

**Behavior:** The Speed Class feature governs the selection and configuration of high-speed modes as described in sections 5.4 (Bus Speed Modes) and 6.6.2-6.6.4, including HS200 timing mode selection, power class selection (6.6.5), and the sampling tuning procedures (6.6.7) required to achieve reliable high-speed data transfers. It ensures the device meets minimum sequential write performance thresholds critical for applications like video recording and real-time data streaming.

features.name: Electrical Interface
features.description:
## Electrical Interface (F_ELECTRICAL)

The Electrical Interface feature defines the fundamental electrical characteristics and signaling requirements for communication between the e•MMC device and host controller. This includes voltage levels, signal timing parameters, I/O driver specifications, and electrical compatibility requirements across different bus speed modes (such as HS200). As a P0 priority feature, it establishes the essential hardware-level foundation that enables reliable data transmission, proper signal integrity, and interoperability between e•MMC devices and host systems operating at various speeds and voltage configurations.
